heading: A tray icon
body:
`tac.application.tray` in `client/manifest.json` puts an icon in the system tray: the menu bar extras at the top right on macOS, the notification area on Windows, and the StatusNotifierItem area on Linux. `icon` names a PNG file in the client bundle, from 16 to 1024 pixels on each edge and at most 1 MiB; the build stops with `TY1601` when the built bundle has no such file. `tooltip` defaults to the app name. With `template`, the macOS menu bar tints the icon for light and dark mode, so draw it in black on a transparent background; Windows and Linux show its own colors.

The tray menu always starts with Open and ends with Quit (Exit on Windows), so the window can always come back and the app can always stop. Between them are your `items`, which have the same shape as menu items: an `id`, a `label` and exactly one of `route` or `action`, without a `shortcut`. A route item opens the window and then its page. An action item calls a method of an application service, as a menu action does, and is checked the same way (`TY1370`). There are at most 32 tray items, and their ids must differ from the ids of the File, View and Help items. On Windows a click on the icon opens the window and the right button opens the menu; on Linux, the desktop decides which click does what.

With `closeHidesWindow`, closing the window hides it instead. The page and its services keep running, and Open shows the same page again. With `dock: false`, a macOS app runs from the menu bar only and has no Dock icon. Windows and Linux have no Dock, so the build prints a note there.

iOS and Android have no tray, so they refuse `tac.application.tray` with `TY1601`. Linux shows the icon only on a desktop with a tray host, such as KDE Plasma, Xfce, Cinnamon or Ubuntu's GNOME; plain GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension. Without a tray host the build cannot know in advance, so the Linux app keeps its window: closing it quits as before. The Linux tray is tested by running the real GTK host against a test tray host, and the Windows tray code runs under Wine; the macOS and Windows desktop runs are still owed (ADR 0107).
